title: Versioned policy: rules that decide, and decisions that survive
note: The policy layer is what makes 'which rules allowed this' answerable. Each mutation here removes one property that answer depends on: deny-overrides, the default-deny fallthrough, conjunctive matching, gap-free versioning, non-retroactivity, and the refusal to publish a document whose content does not match its claimed digest. P4 is the sharpest -- if in_force_at returns today's policy, every historical decision is re-judged under rules that did not exist when it was made, and I5 means nothing. P18 was REMOVED as equivalent, not because it survived: swapping _recheck_decision's in_force_at(ev.seq) for in_force() is a no-op, because apply() is only ever reached in log order -- load() replays oldest-first and both write paths apply the event they just appended -- so only versions published at or before ev.seq have been folded when the re-check runs. The property it appeared to test is P4's, and P4 is killed. The equivalence is asserted by a test over the call sites rather than by this sentence.
